# Origami

> A local server for large mixture-of-experts models on Apple Silicon Macs: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (the main, most
> tested path; text and images), GLM-5.3-Flash and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (text only). The model stays on disk; Origami
> keeps the always-used weights in memory and reads the experts each token needs from the SSD. One native Swift/Metal
> binary (`origami`) that speaks the OpenAI, Anthropic and Ollama APIs. Tested on three Macs so far: an M2 Pro with
> 32 GB on macOS 26, an M1 MacBook Air with 16 GB on macOS 27 (slow) and a user's M4 Max with 128 GB (about 30 tok/s). Needs macOS 15+ and 24 GB of memory or more (`origami setup` refuses under 16 GB).

## Key facts

- Start: `origami setup`, then `origami serve` (port 11439), then `origami dashboard`. `origami help <command>` shows
  a command's options.
- Base URL `http://127.0.0.1:11439/v1`. Endpoints: `POST /v1/chat/completions`, `POST /v1/responses` (no
  `previous_response_id`), `POST /v1/messages`, `POST /v1/messages/count_tokens`, Ollama `POST /api/chat`,
  `POST /api/generate`, `GET /api/tags`, `POST /api/show`, `GET /api/ps`, `GET /api/version`; `GET /v1/models`,
  `GET /health`, `GET /v1/status`, `GET /dashboard`.
- Model name: by default one model, `origami`, and any name gets the model chosen in the dashboard. With
  `list_models true` every model is listed and a request naming another one loads it (one model loaded at a time).
- Exact by default: replies are the model's own. Faster levels are opt-in and change replies: `dynamic` and `fast` on
  every model, and `fastest` on Qwen (`faster` still means `fast`). Per request `"origami_mode": "<level>"` or `<model>-<level>`;
  `allow_fast false` forbids them. An exact request never reuses fast-mode state.
- One request runs at a time; up to 64 wait. Use streaming: SSE streams send `: keepalive` every 10 s, and a
  non-streamed request whose client closes its sending side is treated as gone. Set client timeouts to 10 minutes or
  more.
- Context: `context`, default 8k, up to 262144. Coding agents need 32k or more.
- Thinking: `reasoning_effort` (`none` … `max`) or `max_thinking_tokens`; the server default is `none`.
- Saved prompts are reused across turns and restarts (`usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`); `X-Origami-Keep`
  pins a session; `"prompt_cache_policy": "no_store"` skips saving.
- Settings: `origami config` lists them; `origami config set <key> <value>`. File:
  `~/Library/Application Support/Origami/config.json` (`--config` or `ORIGAMI_CONFIG` names another). Named models:
  `models.json` in the data folder (`data_dir`, default `~/Library/Application Support/Origami`). Order: flag, then
  `ORIGAMI_<KEY>` variable, then the named model's own value, then the settings file.
- API key: off by default; `api_key` makes every request send `Authorization: Bearer <key>` or `x-api-key`.
  Listens on 127.0.0.1 unless `listen lan`.
- Problems: `origami doctor` says what to fix; `origami report` prints a block for a GitHub issue; the last 50 log
  lines are in `/v1/status` `events`.
